ns_planet_of_the_apes.blurb: A cluster of boulders on the shore of Digby Neck, facing the Bay of Fundy, in the Sandy Cove area. Eighteen problems are recorded here, all bouldering, and the field is known as the densest concentration of boulders in the region. Most lines fall between V0 and V4, with a handful of V1 and V2 problems to warm up on and a single problem near V6 for the strong. The stone is clean, grippy basalt. Getting in means travelling along the shoreline over rocks rather than on a trail, so wear sturdy shoes. Expect a quiet, uncrowded place; many more problems exist here than are listed.
ns_planet_of_the_apes.parking_note: Drive to the end of Bay Road in the village of Sandy Cove, off Route 217, and leave the car out of the way near the old pier.
ns_planet_of_the_apes.approach: From the end of Bay Road, pick your way over the shoreline rocks, passing the old pier, and keep following the coast to the boulder field.

ns_gibraltar_rock.blurb: A granite cliff near Musquodoboit Harbour, set in open hemlock woods with a calm, quiet feel. The base is often in shade. Seventeen routes split almost evenly between trad (nine) and sport (eight), spanning easy 5.5 terrain up to 5.12 testpieces. A warm-up wall sits at the left end and the hardest lines are on the right, beyond a wooden ladder at the base. There is a mix of single pitches and at least one longer two-pitch route, so it suits a varied day with a mixed-ability party. Reaching the base means a short, trail-less scramble uphill through the trees.

ns_howe_crag.blurb: A granite crag in the Musquodoboit area inland from Halifax, made up of two walls. It is mainly a trad venue (fifteen of sixteen routes), with some top-rope lines and one sport route, running from 5.6 up to a single route at the 5.12 level. Most of the grades sit in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The granite is sharp and sticky, as is typical of the region. It catches somewhat more breeze than the neighbouring Columbus Wall, which means fewer bugs. Anchors are mostly trees or placed gear, and a few lines have rings, so bring a standard rack.

ns_chebucto_head.blurb: A coastal headland about half an hour from downtown Halifax, just beyond the mouth of the harbour, where a lighthouse sits on a steep cliff well used by local climbers. Fifteen problems and routes are recorded: eight boulder problems from V0 to about V4, mostly in the middle and upper part of that range, plus six sport routes from easy 5th class up to 5.11 and one trad line. The granite is sharp and the boulders are on a short walk-in. Surf matters, since some boulders become unsafe when the swell is up, so check conditions and bring pads, shoes and chalk.

ns_virginia_slab.blurb: A small slab close to Halifax, no more than about 15 metres tall, with mostly bolted lines plus a few trad routes. Of the fifteen climbs, ten are sport and five are trad, graded from easy 5th class to 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The white granite has small crystals and pebbles that stick out, giving good friction for technical, balancy slab climbing, though holds can be sparse and the pitches feel sustained. A short, discreet trail leads in from the end of a residential street and arrives at the top of the cliff before descending to the base.
